problem: VLA navigation models give semantically plausible paths but ignore embodiment-specific mobility constraints, so a path feasible for one robot may be infeasible for another. Candidate-selection methods such as VAMOS can only choose among a finite set of proposals, and embodiment-aware refinement needs costly supervision.
motivation: Heterogeneous robots (wheeled, legged) need different feasible routes for the same goal. Coupling semantics, embodiment and control in one end-to-end model makes adaptation hard. A 2D pixel-space trace can act as a common interface, spatially aligned with visual traversability cues, that decouples semantic proposal from physical grounding.
key_idea: Propose an embodiment-agnostic pixel-space trace with a VLA (VL-Tracer), then refine it with an embodiment-conditioned residual adapter (CE-Adapter) trained on planner-generated (CE-RRT*) traces from segmentation-based cost maps.
insight: Removing CE-Adapter drops the NaviTrace total score from 45.68 to 22.56, with the largest losses on physically grounded categories (accessibility -3.18 vs 33.79, social norms 1.28 vs 37.87). This shows the residual refinement does more than smooth the trace. Scores are also balanced across embodiments (42-46). Providing a goal pixel raises the score to 63.91, so the pixel interface uses precise goals well.
method: VL-Tracer: OmniVLA-based (Llama 7B) VLA with LoRA fine-tuning on VAMOS trace data; inputs are RGB, language and/or goal pixel with modality dropout (p=0.3); a tanh MLP head outputs N=8 normalized waypoints in [-1,1]^2; MSE + smoothness loss

CE-Adapter: ResNet visual encoder modulated at each stage by FiLM from a learned robot embedding; a Transformer over visual tokens plus a robot token; trace queries from T_init cross-attend to the visual tokens; the residual head outputs delta_max*tanh offsets, giving T_e = T_init + ΔT
Auxiliary heads: a traversability reconstruction head predicts the cost map, and a sensitivity head gives a per-embodiment cost weight alpha_e (softplus of an MLP on the robot embedding)

CE-RRT*: Mask2Former panoptic segmentation is turned into a per-embodiment cost map (free/soft/obstacle classes plus distance-transform clearance penalties); RRT* in the image plane (10k iterations, step 25 px) gives cost-minimizing reference traces, resampled to 8 waypoints

Training objective: two-stage training with VL-Tracer frozen afterwards; CE-Adapter loss = trace MSE to CE-RRT* reference + cost map reconstruction + alpha_e-weighted cost at waypoints + second-order smoothness; 62k images, 64x64 input, Adam lr 1e-4; inference needs no segmentation or cost map

Real-world deployment: RGB is sent by WiFi from a Jetson Orin to an RTX 4090 workstation, and the returned trace is converted to local waypoints for a closed-loop controller on wheeled and legged robots

setting.backbone: OmniVLA-based VL-Tracer (Llama 7B, LoRA fine-tuned) + CE-Adapter (ResNet + Transformer, trained from scratch on a pretrained ResNet)
setting.training_data: VL-Tracer: VAMOS navigation trace data (LoRA, 8xA100, ~48h); CE-Adapter: 62k egocentric navigation images auto-labeled by CE-RRT* for wheeled/legged (and other) embodiments
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (plus language and/or goal pixel)
setting.action_space: 8 normalized 2D image-plane waypoints (pixel-space trace), projected to local waypoints for a fixed low-level controller
setting.privileged: none at test time (segmentation and cost maps only used for training labels)

numbers.extra: language + embodiment input; trained on VAMOS traces and 62k CE-RRT* images

results: CrossTracer scores 45.68 on NaviTrace, beating Gemini-2.5-Pro (35.67, +10.01, +28%) and Robobrain-2.5-8B (27.96). Without CE-Adapter it scores 22.56, and with a goal pixel it reaches 63.91. In real-world tests it beats OmniVLA on wheeled (SR 0.65 vs 0.40) and legged (SR 0.70 vs 0.45) robots.
limitations: Relies on panoptic segmentation, so segmentation errors corrupt the cost maps and reference traces
Per-embodiment cost map configurations are hand-specified, requiring expertise for new robots
2D pixel traces have no 3D structure (overhangs, height discontinuities) and there is no closed-loop replanning; real-world evaluation is small (5 trials per task, only OmniVLA as baseline)
